reasons.builder: Sonnet for quota. It is a one-line change plus text, small enough to finish before slice 1's tasks reach project_checks.py.

design:
Decision 1: the line is the existing 'fast' flag, not a new setting. The operator already marks which checks a completion waits for, and those are the ones a delay hurts. A per-check priority setting was not added: one more knob for a distinction the project already states.

Decision 2: CPU-time limits were considered in the roadmap and rejected there in favour of this simpler change.

Decision 3: priority stays out of the check's digest, as today, so a pass at either priority is reused.

lifecycle: Exploring until the operator approves it. It builds in parallel with slice 1: it touches only the priority line and the setting's text. Once built, the requirement below-user-priority in 'checks-know-their-phase-and-give-way-to-the-user' is superseded by this document's narrower one.
problem: Since 2026-11-04 the setting 'Checks give way to me' starts every check process below normal priority (hub/hub/project_checks.py:163 gives every check the project's flag; :530-547 applies it). On 2026-11-05, with three tasks building in parallel on the operator's machine, quick checks (ruff, black, each with a 120 s limit) were starved: one ruff run printed 'All checks passed!' and then ran past its limit, and that timeout was blamed on a task (fixed separately as AW-39). A fast check is the one an agent's completion waits on, so slowing it holds a running agent and its turn, not just a background job. The full suite is what is heavy, and is what should give way.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-05 (roadmap approval): a fast check is what an agent's completion waits on, so slowing it holds a running turn; on 2026-11-05 a starved ruff run timed out after passing.
requirements.statement: While the project's 'checks give way to the user' setting is on, every process a check marked fast starts, including the processes those start, runs at the same scheduling priority as it would with the setting off. Every process a check not marked fast starts runs below the priority of a normally started user application, as before.
The 'Checks give way to me' setting's description says that checks marked fast keep normal priority and only the other checks give way.

in_scope: Which checks run below normal priority while a project's checks give way
The setting's description in project settings
non_goals: Changing what 'fast' means, or which checks an agent's completion waits for
Time limits based on CPU time
Changing the setting's default (off) or the opt-out rule priority-opt-out
Making checks faster or the suite smaller

summary: When a project's checks give way to the user, only the longer checks do. Checks marked fast, which an agent's completion waits for, run at normal priority, so a busy machine slows the full suite but not the quick gate every task passes through. This is slice 3 of 'Checks any project can use, judged against a known-failing list'. It narrows the approved requirement below-user-priority of 'checks-know-their-phase-and-give-way-to-the-user', which put every check process below normal priority.
